request: What impact did passing Obamacare have on the federal budget?

reply.reply:
**The ACA was designed to fund expanded coverage partly through new health-related revenues projected at about $392 billion over 10 years; the evidence reviewed here does not establish its total net effect on the federal deficit.**

- The ACA’s health-related revenue provisions were projected to raise about $392 billion over 10 years to pay for expanded health insurance coverage. (R41128, PDF p. 2)
- CBO and JCT projected $391.7 billion in health-related revenues over 10 years. (R41128, PDF p. 4)
- Federal premium tax credit expenditures were larger under the later ARPA/FY2022 Reconciliation rules than under ACA-only rules. (R48290, PDF p. 7)

Not yet covered: A full original-enactment estimate comparing total spending increases and revenue increases (net deficit effect) is not established by the findings gathered; only health-related revenues and later subsidy comparison are documented.
reply.reasoning: CRS reports the ACA’s health-related revenue provisions were projected to raise about $392 billion over 10 years. This alone does not answer whether the law’s total spending and revenues increased or reduced the deficit; the later CRS report only says premium-credit expenditures were larger under subsequent enhanced-subsidy rules than under ACA-only rules.
